circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the traditional season finale for Formula One since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue to host a Grand Prix, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Melbourne's Albert Park Circuit is a street-based track that encircles a lakeside park in the city's Albert Park suburb. It hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various supporting racing events, holding the highest FIA safety classification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and renaming, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before establishing itself as the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that same year. Beyond Formula One, the track accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and 24-hour endurance competitions, while holding FIA Grade 1 certification and offering multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations that test all aspects of driver skill. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates 140,700 spectators and regularly hosts the Spanish Grand Prix as a key fixture on the Formula One calendar.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This 7. 004 km Belgian circuit in the Ardennes region has hosted the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, making it one of racing's most historic venues. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix status from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, establishing itself as a permanent fixture on the modern F1 calendar.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km street circuit that serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has also been used for various other racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing series events alongside its primary Formula One commitment.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated in Northamptonshire that has served as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, having first hosted the event in 1948. The track gained particular significance when it staged the inaugural World Championship round in 1950, marking the beginning of Formula One's championship era. Beyond Formula One, the facility also accommodates MotoGP racing.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the sport's inaugural Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. Originally envisioned as a street course within Budapest's main park, the track was ultimately constructed outside the city near a major highway and completed in record time, taking just eight months from its October 1985 start date.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km speedway constructed in 1922 that ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues. It has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a brief closure in 1980 for renovation, making it one of the few circuits to appear on every Formula One calendar since the championship's inception, and earns its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its characteristically long straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track has established itself as a premier destination for both Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that snakes through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout traverses past famous landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, transforming the city's main commercial boulevard into a racing venue for Formula One competition.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit honours the Rodríguez brothers, both accomplished drivers who tragically lost their lives in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards after a 23-year absence, resuming on its current layout following earlier hosting periods that concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by specialist track architects, it was created for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022, and has since been adapted for other motorsport series.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the urban landscape of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encompassing the harbour area of the Principality of Monaco. Though officially designated by its full name, the venue is widely known simply as "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Grade 1 facility situated north of Doha in Qatar, measuring 5. 419 kilometers with a principal straight spanning 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years prior. The venue hosts a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue in Saudi Arabia that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021. The track runs along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah and began accommodating electric single-seater racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its urban racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit features a balanced blend of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for comprehensive vehicle evaluation. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major international motorsport events including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship. The track's versatile layout has accommodated various racing series over the years, from IndyCar to sports car championships across multiple continents.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British motorsport competitor who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons and secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso is the sole driver to have won both the Formula One World Drivers' Championship and the World Endurance Championship, achieving the latter in 2018–19 while also capturing two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, made his Formula One debut in 2025 with Mercedes, where he currently races. He has already secured eight Grand Prix victories during his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas in the championship series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing the Audi team in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that has yielded 10 Grand Prix victories. His most notable achievements include finishing second in the drivers' championship on two occasions during his Mercedes years in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has appeared in seven Formula One races between 2024 and 2025 while holding a reserve role at Haas. Beyond his limited F1 appearances, he actively competes in European Le Mans Series prototype racing for Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri stands as a significant achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian racing driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding the joint-record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive experience from both single-seater and endurance racing backgrounds. Beyond his Formula One career, he achieved a significant milestone by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved significant success including a championship runner-up finish in 2022 and nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish motorsport competitor, has transitioned from his Formula One career, which spanned 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, to compete as a factory driver for BMW in the World Endurance Championship with WRT. He also races part-time in NASCAR's top series for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British Formula One driver for McLaren, claimed the world championship title in 2025 and has secured 13 Grand Prix victories during his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One, bringing with him a significant career highlight from his time with Alpine, where he secured victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Cadillac. The veteran driver finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren, has secured nine Formula One victories throughout his four-year career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by his "Honey Badger" nickname, competed in Formula One for 14 seasons beginning in 2011 before retiring in 2024. He secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured eight victories in Formula One across his multi-season career with Mercedes, where he currently competes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who most recently competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He has since transitioned to endurance racing, currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition after previously racing in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive world championships with Red Bull Racing between 2021 and 2024, establishing himself as one of the sport's dominant forces with 73 race victories across his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He continues his involvement with the sport in a supporting capacity for the American team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone base since 2021, Alpine has served as Renault's official Formula One representative, initially rebranded from the Renault F1 Team to highlight the Alpine sports car marque. The squad maintained this works partnership until Renault's planned departure from the sport at the conclusion of the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive marque, has maintained an on-and-off presence in Formula One across multiple eras, with its contemporary incarnation operating under the corporate structure of AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished outfit, fielding cars in every championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Identified by their iconic prancing horse emblem, the team has established an enduring legacy of success that distinguishes them from all other competitors in the championship.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas in 2014, the team commenced racing in 2016. Leadership transitioned from its founding principal to Ayao Komatsu in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established by Peter Sauber in 1970, the team initially competed in endurance motorsport before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. Over three decades in the sport, it underwent numerous transformations and became the fourth-longest-tenured constructor by race entries before departing in 2025, when Audi acquired its operations to establish its own F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership. The team competes under sponsorship arrangements in the sport's premier championship.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a manufacturer and team operator, with its current iteration based in Brackley and holding a German racing licence. The team, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, gained additional ownership structure in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing program is traditionally identified by the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents Red Bull GmbH's dual constructor strategy in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister outfit within the Red Bull organization's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but racing under an Austrian licence, has been a dominant Formula One force since its 2005 establishment by energy drink conglomerate Red Bull GmbH. The team experienced sustained success under longtime principal Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, when Laurent Mekies assumed leadership of the squad, which forms part of Red Bull's two-team racing operation.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Atlassian Williams F1 Team represents a prominent British Formula One outfit established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's prior unsuccessful racing venture. The constructor operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, where it has developed and fielded competitive single-seater machinery throughout its lengthy championship history.
